      <h1>The Coordination Tax Calculator: When Does Orchestration Pay?</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">A defensible cost model and a go/no-go threshold for multi-agent orchestration on this codebase — plus an honest statement of what the investment buys: quality and reduced context degradation, not elapsed time.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-17-coordination-tax-calculator</b><br>
      Pack D - Architecture and ownership<br>
      fill order <b>7</b> &middot; type <b>calculator</b><br>
      audience <b>mixed</b>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-source">

    Locator: "Multi-agent orchestration saves time through parallelism and improves quality through focused context"
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Start with the completed <b>WS-17-orchestration-topology-selector</b>. Measure one real change, not an average; enter the time the orchestrator actually spent, and state which activities your organisation counts as coordination before calculating overhead. Use the grey italic column only as a single-case prior, not a target. If you are forecasting because no execution exists yet, mark the basis as Forecast and schedule the re-run against actuals.     <div class="ws-meta"><b>WS-17-coordination-tax-calculator</b><br>Pack D - Architecture and ownership<br>fill order <b>7</b> &middot; type <b>calculator</b><br>audience <b>mixed</b></div>

      <tbody>
        <tr><td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">28</span></td><td><b>First-run multiplier applied?</b></td><td class="prior"><div class="prior--hedged"><span class="hedge-figure">Roughly 3×.</span><span class="hedge-text">"Your first time through will take roughly 3×."</span><span class="hedge-src">handbook\ch18-the-execution-meta-process.qmd L188</span></div><small>The reference timing reflects an experienced practitioner with battle-tested instruction files, established personas and conventions already externalised into the codebase.</small></td><td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>Applied when field 5 reads First</span><div class="ours-label">Our own multiplier, once available</div><span class="f-text sm"></span></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">29</span></td><td><b>What the first run buys</b></td><td class="prior">Reference: the first run is an investment in infrastructure — instruction files, partition boundaries, wave-sizing intuition — that makes every subsequent run faster.<span class="prior-src">ch18 L188</span></td><td class="fill"><span class="f-box"></span><small>Our answer.</small></td></tr>
        <tr><td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">30</span></td><td><b>Planning-time trend across runs</b></td><td class="prior">Reference: the second run takes half the planning time; by the third the dispatch prompts are templates.<span class="prior-src">ch17 L376</span></td><td class="fill"><span class="f-box"></span><small>Our observed trend.</small></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
